subject: BAA vs SOC2 scoping: hosting recommendation & procurement path
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Simon <laura.simon@careliahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: BAA vs SOC2 scoping: hosting recommendation & procurement path

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single thread to track decisions.

Summary of needs you shared:
- PHI storage for adult patient summaries and clinician notes (encrypted at rest, retention 7 years)
- Audit logs for access and model prompts for specific diagnostic flows
- High throughput during business hours (bursty inference for triage) with predictable latency
- Legal needs a BAA and procurement timeline, security wants SOC 2 artifacts and a network diagram

Redwood recommendation (high level):
- Primary: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) paired with a BAA — gives predictable throughput and separation of customer data from shared tenancy.
- Option: Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) if your legal/risk team requires customer-managed keys (HSM) or complete control of private network for audits.
- Not recommended: Hosted multi-tenant API for this scope unless you are comfortable with our Dedicated isolation and the BAA language (cost advantage but less control).

Information and artifacts we can provide right away:
1) SOC 2 Type II attestation copy and scope summary (redacted) — see attached summary questions to confirm what level of evidence your auditors will need.
2) BAA standard template + trackable redlines (we can accept limited redlines; attached sample).
3) VPC/network diagram and list of required ports for Private deployment.
4) KMS/HSM options: we support Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed AWS KMS with BYOK for Dedicated and Private modes.

Action items / proposed timeline:
- Laura / Alan: confirm whether Carelia requires customer-managed keys + on-prem network access for initial pilot (reply by Wed 10/20).
- Security sync: Naomi offered to run a 45-min technical deep-dive for your security team; propose Thu 10/21 morning PT.
- Procurement: I will loop in Sales Ops after you confirm hosting preference so we can pull together a quote and draft SOW.

Attachments: SOC2_summary_questions.pdf (short checklist), BAA_template_redlines.docx (sample)

If that aligns I'll schedule the security deep-dive and send a short mutual action plan.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0194

---
Note: Redwood Dedicated supports prefix caching, continuous batching, and can reserve GPUs for predictable p99 latency under the observed triage workload.

From: Laura Simon <laura.simon@careliahealth.com>

Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BAA vs SOC2 scoping: hosting recommendation & procurement path

Thanks Hannah — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) KMS: for the pilot we prefer customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS with CMKs). Long term we may require HSM for PHI in production; need to confirm with infra.
2) Audit logs: we need per-request prompt capture and immutable retention for 3 years initially (could extend). Is that exportable to our Splunk/CloudWatch?
3) SOC2: our auditors will need the last two Type II reports and the control matrix mapping. Is the attestation you provide redacted?

Procurement: I’ve looped in Alan (Procurement) — Alan, would you prefer an initial pilot agreement (30 days) followed by a purchase order for a 6-mo reserved capacity, or go straight to a 6-mo reserved contract? We can move quickly if legal and security are satisfied.

We are available for Naomi's security deep-dive Thu 10/21 9–11am PT.

Laura Simon
VP, Clinical Product | Carelia Health

Laura / Hannah — quick technical notes to help Procurement and Security: 

1) Customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS): Supported for Dedicated and Private VPC modes. For Dedicated we can enable envelope encryption where the data plane keys are customer-managed CMKs; control plane remains Redwood-managed (standard). For Private VPC we can offer full BYOK with an HSM-backed CMK if required.

2) Audit logs & exports: We can stream immutable request logs (timestamp, request id, prompt hash) to your CloudWatch/S3 or provide S3 export snapshots shipped to your Splunk ingest role. Retention policy is configurable; default export includes system and application-level entries.

3) SOC 2 artifacts: We can provide the last SOC 2 Type II report (2026) with redactions and a controls mapping spreadsheet. For auditors requiring evidence (e.g., change management, incident logs) we can organize an evidence package; expect a 3–5 business day turnaround for curated artifacts once scope is confirmed.

4) Network & segmentation: Attached is a draft network_diagram_vpc.pdf showing recommended egress controls and peering for Private deployment. For Dedicated you will typically use an IP allowlist + VPC peering for secure traffic — we can lock down ports and apply mutual TLS.

Procurement options and rough lead times: 
- Pilot (30 days, Dedicated capacity): ~1–2 business days to provision, quote in 24 hours after PO.
- 6-mo Reserved (Dedicated): provisioning included; contract and legal review ~7–14 business days depending on redlines.
- Private VPC/on-prem: architecture and ops prep typically adds 2–6 weeks depending on network/ops approvals.

I’m attaching a sample BAA with our standard redlines to accelerate Legal review. If you confirm pilot + CMK, I’ll prepare a quote and SOW.

Attachments: BAA_template_redlines.docx, network_diagram_vpc.pdf

—Karthik
